entries.name: HiRISE stereo DTM ESP_023524_1985 / ESP_023379_1985, Jezero crater
entries.publisher: University of Arizona HiRISE / NASA MRO
entries.taken: Elevation raster DTEEC_023524_1985_023379_1985_U01.IMG: 21258 x 8235 pixels, 1.0097 m/px, float32 metres above the Mars 2000 datum, valid range -2694.83 to -2510.19 m. We read only a window over HTTP range requests (the server supports them, checked 2026-11-06).
entries.use: Every site-scale number: elevation, slope, roughness, hazard classes, route cost, 3D view.
entries.status: Downloaded by the team (window) and header read; page confirms Jezero, centre 18.3°N 77.53°E.

entries.name: MSR Terrain-Relative-Navigation HiRISE DTM and ortho mosaics, Jezero
entries.taken: Candidate: 1 m/px DTM mosaic with confidence layer (5.3 GB zip), Jezero lat 18.135 to 18.588, lon 77.057 to 77.380.
entries.use: Not used yet. Preferred later for a wider, explicitly Jezero-controlled terrain and an uncertainty layer.
entries.status: Page read only.

entries.name: MGS MOLA MEGDR topography, 4 pixel/degree (global)
entries.publisher: NASA PDS Geosciences Node, from the MOLA Team
entries.taken: 720 x 1440 big-endian int16, metres above the GMM3 areoid, 0.25 degree pixels, lat +90 at top, lon 0..360 from the left (checked against the PDS label).
entries.use: Globe elevation layer (2 x 2 block mean to the 0.5 degree grid), and pressure and radiation derived from it.
entries.status: Label read by the team's assistant; file downloaded by scripts/build_globe.py on your machine (about 2 MB). Replaces the earlier 463 m candidate for the globe.

entries.name: Mars 2020 MEDA calibrated environmental data (CAL_ATS air temperature, CAL_PS pressure)
entries.taken: Per-sol CSV files. CAL_ATS: ATS_LOCAL_TEMP1..5 in kelvin. CAL_PS: BAROCAP1..3_PRESSURE in pascal, version 2.0 (reprocessed for drift, 2021-10-29). Units confirmed from the PDS4 labels.
entries.use: Air temperature mean and daily swing for the sol planner; pressure baseline.
entries.status: Folder listings and sol 1 labels read by the team; sol 100 columns read; sampled sols downloaded by the team.

entries.name: Odyssey GRS special product: epithermal neutron flux ns_epithermal_020917
entries.publisher: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Feldman et al. 2002, Science 297:75-78)
entries.taken: 259,200 text rows 'lon, lat, flux' (counts/s), one per 0.5 degree cell, lon 0..360. Less flux means more hydrogen. First 25.7 days of mapping only. Rows with flux exactly 0.000 are treated as no data (our reading).
entries.use: Globe hydrogen proxy layer epithermal_cps, scored between its 5th and 95th percentile (team choice, written to config/scoring.json by scripts/build_globe.py).
entries.status: Label and first rows read by the team's assistant; table downloaded by scripts/build_globe.py on your machine. Not calibrated to water-equivalent hydrogen; seasonal CO2 frost mixes in at high latitude. A full-mission water-equivalent hydrogen map would be better: no verified PDS file found yet.

entries.name: Mars Trek MOLA colourised shaded relief tiles
entries.taken: Image tiles, scheme {z}/{row}/{col}.jpg, 2^(z+1) columns by 2^z rows, row 0 at the north.
entries.use: Optional global basemap.
entries.status: Tiles z0 and z1 opened by the team. Maximum zoom and cross-site (CORS) use untested.

entries.name: Derived Jezero air temperatures from MEDA ATS, first 700 sols
entries.taken: Per-sol CSV of derived temperatures (Fourier fits).
entries.use: Candidate to replace the sinusoid in the sol planner.
entries.status: Record opened by the team; not used yet.

entries.name: MEDA surface pressure at Jezero, sols 1 to 414
entries.taken: Pressure in Pa, 32 files, 67 MB; accuracy under 3.5 Pa.
entries.use: Candidate cross-check of the MEDA pressure we compute.
entries.status: Page read; not used yet.

entries.name: Minetti et al. 2002, Energy cost of walking and running at extreme uphill and downhill slopes
entries.taken: Cw(i) = 280.5 i^5 - 58.7 i^4 - 76.8 i^3 + 51.9 i^2 + 19.6 i + 2.5 J/(kg m), valid for slopes i from -0.45 to +0.45; 10 athletes, treadmill, no load.
entries.use: Energy per metre of walking at every slope (physics.py). Slope part scaled by g_Mars/g_Earth. The tests reproduce the paper's Table 2.
entries.status: Paper supplied by the team. Earth data: using it on Mars is a hypothesis.

entries.name: Cavagna, Willems and Heglund 2000, The role of gravity in human walking
entries.taken: External mechanical work minimum 0.30 J/(kg m) at 1 g (4.5 km/h) and 0.15 at 0.4 g (2.5 km/h); best pendular recovery speed 5.5, 3.5 and about 6.5 km/h at 1, 0.4 and 1.5 g.
entries.use: Flat-ground cost factor 0.75 and the pace of 3.4 km/h (speed proportional to the square root of gravity).
entries.status: Paper supplied by the team. Mechanical work, not metabolic; three men; no suit. The DOI is from memory: check it.

entries.name: Apollo 16 Time and Motion Study (NASA MSC M72-6)
entries.taken: Suited astronaut metabolic power on the Moon: walking at about 3 ft/s, 1112 to 1185 BTU/h (326 to 347 W); carrying 41 lb, up to 2300 BTU/h (674 W).
entries.use: Default sustained power (326 W) and a pace cross-check (3 ft/s = 3.3 km/h).
entries.status: Report supplied by the team. Several values were damaged in the PDF text: re-check against the page images. It analysed no slope effect.

entries.name: Soule and Goldman 1972; Pandolf, Givoni and Goldman 1977, terrain coefficients
entries.taken: Earth terrain factors: blacktop 1.0, dirt road 1.1, light brush 1.2, heavy brush 1.5, swampy bog 1.8, loose sand 2.1, soft snow 15/25/35 cm 2.5/3.3/4.1.
entries.use: Sanity anchor for the rough-ground multiplier (a team hypothesis).
entries.status: Values read on Wikipedia; verify in the papers.

entries.name: Hassler et al. 2013, Mars' surface radiation environment measured with the MSL RAD
entries.taken: 0.67 mSv/day at Gale crater surface (cruise 1.8 mSv/day).
entries.use: Radiation baseline for the globe scoring.
entries.status: Press summary read.

entries.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle design slopes
entries.publisher: Jacob et al., LPSC 57 (2026), NASA NTRS
entries.taken: Design slope 20 to 23° favourable, maximum 25°.
entries.use: Echoed by the 20° (hazardous) and 25° (forbidden) hazard limits. Not a Mars walking limit.
entries.status: Page read.

entries.name: Steepest slope driven by a Mars rover (Opportunity, 32°)
entries.taken: 32° tilt.
entries.use: Hard ceiling for rover-class vehicles.
entries.status: Page read.

entries.name: Allison and McEwen 2000, areocentric solar coordinates and Mars time recipes (Mars24)
entries.publisher: Planetary and Space Science 48:215-235; NASA GISS Mars24
entries.taken: Mars Sol Date from Julian date: MSD = (JD_TT - 2451549.5)/1.0274912517 + 44796.0 - 0.0009626; local mean solar time = MTC + east longitude/15; equation of time and solar longitude Ls from the paper's series (mean anomaly, fictitious mean Sun, 7 planetary perturbation terms); true solar time = mean + EOT.
entries.use: The map clock (web/marsclock.mjs): Jezero local true solar time from Earth time.
entries.status: Coefficients typed from the paper: compare each one with the NASA GISS Mars24 page. Tests: EOT stays within about ±51 min over a year; the Perseverance touchdown (20:44 UTC, signal delay removed) gives about 15:15 true solar time, mid-afternoon as reported (my memory, verify). Leap seconds: 37 s assumed.

entries.name: NASA Mars Fact Sheet (orbit and radiation constants)
entries.taken: Solar irradiance 586.2 W/m2, Bond albedo 0.250, eccentricity 0.0935, obliquity 25.19 deg, mean surface temperature about 214 K.
entries.use: Energy-balance temperature layer (src/mars_survival/thermal.py) and its sanity check.
entries.status: Page read 2026-11-07. Ls of perihelion (251 deg) comes from Allison & McEwen, to verify; emissivity 1 and the 148 K CO2 frost point are our choices, not from that page.

entries.name: Suit and gear mass
entries.taken: 170 kg
entries.use: Unknown for any real Mars suit. User input.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Rough-ground multiplier
entries.taken: 1 + (roughness / 0.25 m)^2; impassable above 1.5 m
entries.use: No Mars source. Earth anchors in P4; HiRISE 1 m/px cannot see boulders.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Hazard class limits
entries.taken: slope 10 / 20 / 25°, roughness 0.25 / 0.6 / 1.5 m
entries.use: No NASA slip or tip limit for a walking human. 20 and 25° echo P6.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Outdoor window rules
entries.taken: sun above 5°, air above -90 °C, dust optical depth below 3
entries.use: Not from a NASA suit specification.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Daily temperature shape
entries.taken: sine wave peaking at 14 h local solar time
entries.use: Simplification; mean and swing come from D4.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Gravity scaling of the slope cost
entries.taken: slope part x g_Mars/g_Earth (0.378)
entries.use: Hypothesis; flat part uses P2. Not tested on Mars or with a suit.
entries.status: Team assumption: replace when a source is found.

entries.name: Flat-site tolerance
entries.taken: A disc 120 m across counts as flat if at most 5% of it exceeds 5° slope or 0.25 m roughness
entries.use: With zero tolerance the first real Jezero build found no flat site at all. No NASA landing-site rule is used; replace with one.
entries.status: Team assumption.

entries.name: Globe: partial scoring and thresholds
entries.taken: Cells are scored when the measured or derived layers carry at least 30% of the total weight (--min-coverage 0.3). Only elevation and epithermal flux are measured; pressure and radiation come from elevation.
entries.use: Without this the real globe would be empty. Pressure and radiation follow elevation, so the score mostly says 'low and hydrogen-rich'. Every cell's coverage is shown.
entries.status: Team assumption: add temperature, thermal inertia, rocks and slope layers, then raise the threshold.

entries.name: Globe temperature processing
entries.taken: Median over Mars years; daily mean = (T03 + T15)/2; swing = T15 - T03; values outside 130-320 K dropped; seasons weighted by duration; 75% of the year required; 5 degree nodes treated as points and interpolated
entries.use: The two local times only approximate the daily mean and the swing (the swing is smaller than the true max minus min). Polar and winter gaps stay empty.
entries.status: Team assumptions. The energy-balance model (src/mars_survival/thermal.py) is kept only as a cross-check.

entries.name: Thermal inertia scoring ramp
entries.taken: score 0 at 100 tiu, 1 at 300 tiu; night map; weights habitat 0.5, landing 1.5
entries.use: No sourced engineering limit yet (landing-site workshop criteria are a candidate). Very high values (bare rock) are not penalised.
entries.status: Team assumption.

entries.name: MGS TES derived thermal inertia maps (Putzig & Mellon 2007)
entries.publisher: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Putzig, Mellon, Heet, Ward; V1.0, 2009)
entries.taken: 3600 x 7200 big-endian int16, 20 pixel/degree, lon -180..180, units J m-2 K-1 s-1/2; derived range 5 to 5000. Night map used. Label, readme and datainfo read by the team's assistant; the label states no scaling or missing value, so raw integers are taken as tiu and values outside 5..5000 as no data.
entries.use: Planet-map layer thermal_inertia_tiu (loose dust versus firm ground), scored 100 to 300 tiu.
entries.status: Downloaded by scripts/build_globe.py on your machine (52 MB). The script warns if the median is outside 50 to 800 tiu.

entries.name: Apollo 15-17 PLSS (portable life support system) consumables
entries.publisher: Wikipedia, summarising NASA documents (secondary; primary: NASA ALSJ, Apollo Flight PLSS)
entries.taken: Design EVA duration: 4 h (Apollo 11-14) and 8 h (Apollo 15-17); battery 390 Wh, cooling water 5.2 L, LiOH 1.42 kg for the J-missions.
entries.use: Suit autonomy (8 h default) of the return-to-shelter calculation.
entries.status: Page read. Secondary source: check the primary NASA ALSJ document (history.nasa.gov/alsj/ALSJ-FlightPLSS.pdf) before publication.

entries.name: NASA TN D-7883, metabolic expenditures for Apollo lunar surface EVA (Table I)
entries.publisher: NASA (hosted by the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal)
entries.taken: Mean total metabolic rate of the listed Apollo EVAs: 930 Btu/h (980 kJ/h) = 272.6 W. Apollo 15-17 individual EVAs: 780 to 1100 Btu/h.
entries.use: Energy budget of the return-to-shelter calculation (mean metabolic rate x usable walking time).
entries.status: Table read. Measured on the Moon, so a hypothesis on Mars.

entries.name: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle: greatest range from the lunar module
entries.taken: Greatest range from the LM: 5.0 km (Apollo 15), 4.5 km (Apollo 16), 7.6 km (Apollo 17).
entries.use: Comparison line shown beside the computed reach. Not an input.
entries.status: Page read.

entries.name: Mars Regional Navigation Satellite System (in-situ navigation and timing at a human Mars landing site)
entries.taken: Concept: relay orbiters broadcast GPS-like ranging signals; relative positioning by differencing two ranges is reported 200 to 400 times more accurate than absolute positioning (simulation).
entries.use: Background for the position-sync idea (docs/SYNC_IDEA.md). Not used in the app.
entries.status: Abstract read.

entries.name: Reserve kept on the walking time
entries.taken: 25% of the suit autonomy is kept unspent (adjustable 0 to 50%).
entries.use: Round-trip limit = autonomy x (1 - reserve). No NASA value was found for Apollo walk-back margins.
entries.status: Team assumption.

entries.name: Mean Apollo metabolic rate as the sustainable walking energy
entries.taken: Round-trip walking energy (Minetti model) must stay under 272.6 W x usable time. Time and energy limits are both applied; the stricter one is reported.
entries.use: Return-to-shelter reach.
entries.status: Team assumption.

entries.name: Antenna heights and radio line of sight
entries.taken: Shelter antenna 3 m, suit antenna 1.8 m above ground (adjustable). Straight line with Mars curvature (radius 3389.5 km); no atmosphere, no antenna pattern, no radio frequency.
entries.use: Line-of-sight layer. Geometry only, not a link budget.
entries.status: Team assumption.

entries.name: Shadow and time-budget model
entries.taken: Shadows: ray march along the sun azimuth on the DTM (no sky light, no cast shadow from beyond the window). Time budget: hourly sun elevation and temperature from the Sun plan (simplified sinusoid fed by MEDA); sunset = sun below 0 degrees; caution below the planner minimum sun elevation (5 degrees); cold = below the planner limit.
entries.use: Time-budget card and shadow layer.
entries.status: Team assumption on simplified models.

entries.name: Mars 2020 Science Investigation CTX DEM Mosaic
entries.publisher: USGS Astrogeology Science Center (F. Calef, 2021), from Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX stereo
entries.taken: 20 m/px GeoTIFF (87 MB), lat 17.58 to 19.29, lon 76.99 to 78.58 (whole Jezero crater region). Product page: https://astrogeology.usgs.gov/search/map/mars_2020_science_investigation_ctx_dem_mosaic. Public domain; the page asks to cite the authors (Calef 2021; Mangold et al. 2021, Science, doi:10.1126/science.abl4051).
entries.use: Overview level of the map (overview.html): hillshade of the whole crater with the 1 m detail windows drawn on it. Not used for routing or hazards.
entries.status: Real data. Vertical datum not named on the page (localised to MOLA); only relative relief is shown.

entries.name: HiRISE orthoimages of the Jezero stereo pair (UA/HiRISE)
entries.taken: Window of the orthorectified RED image (candidates on https://www.uahirise.org/dtm/ESP_023524_1985: RED_A 766 MB, RED_C 60 MB). Measured with scripts/fetch_ortho_window.py --inspect on RED_A: 32938 x 85030 px, pixel 0.2524 m, equirectangular Mars, central meridian 77.53 deg, sphere radius 3 394 839.8 m (written in the file).
entries.use: Optional "Photo" layer (up to 0.25 m/px) to see boulders and texture. Picture only: never used for slope, hazard or routes.
entries.status: Resolution verified (0.25 m/px). Co-registration with the DTM not yet checked on the map: compare the photo with the hillshade.
